'''Tasso Joost Kaper''' (born June 25, 1964) is an American mathematician at [[Boston University]], where he chairs the Department of Mathematics and Statistics. His research concerns [[dynamical system]]s and [[applied mathematics]].<ref name="cv">[http://www.bu.edu/math/files/2014/01/Kaper-CV-deptwebsite.pdf Curriculum vitae], BU Math & Statistics, retrieved 2015-02-08.</ref>

Kaper's father is [[Hans G. Kaper]], a Dutch-born retired mathematician at [[Argonne National Laboratory]].<ref name="argonne"/><ref>Birth data for Hans Kaper from [http://hoogleraren.ub.rug.nl/?page=showPerson&type=hoogleraar&hoogleraar_id=1331&lang=en University of Groningen], retrieved 2015-02-08.</ref>
Tasso Kaper did his undergraduate studies at the [[University of Chicago]], graduating in 1986.<ref name="cv"/> He earned a Ph.D. in 1992 from the [[California Institute of Technology]], under the supervision of [[Stephen Wiggins]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=11885}}</ref> On finishing his doctorate, he joined the faculty at Boston University, where he has remained. He was editor-in-chief of ''SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems'' from 2005 to 2011, when he became department chair.<ref name="cv"/> He is currently an editor-in-chief of the journal [[Nonlinearity (journal)|Nonlinearity]] for the [[Institute of Physics]].

In 2009, both Tasso and Hans Kaper were simultaneously honored as [[fellow]]s of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]].<ref name="argonne">[http://www.anl.gov/articles/three-argonne-mathematicians-recognized-siam-fellows Three Argonne mathematicians recognized as SIAM Fellows], [[Argonne National Laboratory]], retrieved 2015-02-08.</ref> In 2012, Kaper became one of the inaugural fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2015-02-08.</ref>
